newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks end off ahead heavyweight HSBC's results.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end off ahead heavyweight HSBC's results.

text.p: Hong Kong share prices took a tumble on Monday with the banking sector leading the way as investors sold down HSBC Holdings Plc shares ahead of the banking giant's interim results.
The Hang Seng Index slid 119.63 points, or 0.73 percent, to close at 16,259.59. Turnover was a hefty HK$22.65 billion compared with HK$26.98 billion on Friday.
"We are going into the most important results of the year. Banks have had an extremely good run. Why take the risk?" said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"All we are doing is having some healthy profit-taking."
HSBC Holdings posted a 13 percent rise in first-half pretax profit to 2.62 billion after the market closed. London analysts had forecast pretax profit of between 2.32 and 2.48 billion stg.
Its shares fell HK$4.00 to HK$264.00 ahead of the announcement.

Shares in its subsdidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd fell HK$1.50 to HK$111.00. It reported interim net profit of HK$4.98 billion compared with HK$4.35 billion last year. Hang Seng Bank had been expected to post a double-digit rise in interim profit.
Brokers said the tone of the market on Tuesday would be set by the results reports.

Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities, said HSBC should lead the market higher. It rose to a high of HK$279.00 in London, pushing the Hang Seng London Reference Index up 277 points to 16,536 in early trade.
"That obviously means that we are going to have a good day tomorrow. The profit-taking will be reversed and Hongkong Bank in the short term will lead the market higher," said Galbraith.

Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd gained HK$0.75 to HK$27.60. The company said it would pay US$78 million for a 51 percent stake in Barney's Inc and buy US$52 million worth of convertible debt from the U.S. retailer.

Shares in Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd rose HK$0.225 to HK$2.85. The company said that government administrative officials were studying the possibility of a merger between the company and other chemical companies.
China Everbright Technology Ltd gained HK$0.25 to HK$3.05. It said it would take a 10 percent stake in Chevalier OA International Ltd. Chevalier OA shares surged HK$0.49 to HK$1.50.
The red chip China-Affiliated Corporations Index gained 15.43 points, or 0.43 percent, to 3,629.07.
